The lock gave way with barely a sound—child’s play, really. Zade stepped into the dim kitchen, the scent of her lingering in the air, something sweet and warm like vanilla and sleep. His gloved fingers traced the edge of the counter, possessive, already imagining her standing there. Unaware. Perfect.

*She’ll find it soon.*  

A single black rose, still dewy from the night’s chill, laid deliberately beside a bottle of *Château Lafite*—*her* favorite, though she’d only mentioned it once, months ago, to a friend over the phone. He remembered. Of course he did.  

His phone was in his hand before he could stop himself, thumb hovering over the keys. The message was simple, but the implication? *Delicious.*  

The text he sent was simple: *"The ’82 is a good year."*  

A pause. His teeth grazed his bottom lip, sharp enough to sting. *Should he say more?* No. Let her wonder. Let her *ache.*  

The shadows swallowed him whole as he slipped back out the way he came, but not before his gaze lingered on the staircase—*her* bedroom just above.  

*Soon.*  Zade locked up behind himself before lighting a cigarette and beginning the trek back to his car, hidden in the woods a quarter mile away.

He'd been texting the little mouse more than usual tonight. Perhaps the whisky had loosened his restraint. From his vantage point in the shadows, Zade drank in the way her fingers trembled over the keyboard - that delicious hesitation he'd come to crave. His thumb traced the edge of his phone as he watched her breath catch when another message lit up her screen.  

**Me:** *"You always bite your lip like that when you're concentrating. Cute. Dangerous."*  

The way her spine stiffened sent a thrill through him. Those wide, pretty eyes darted to the window. *Look harder, little mouse.* The shadows clung to him like old friends, but he allowed the porchlight to flicker at just the right moment - giving her the barest glimpse of movement, just enough to make her pulse jump.  

**Me:** *"Turn off the lamp by the window. I prefer you in moonlight."*  

When she didn't move, his lips curled into a sharp grin. *Stubborn thing.* His fingers flew across the screen again, not giving her time to decide between fight or flight.  

**Me:** *"Don't call the police, little mouse. They won't get here in time."*  

A lie, of course. He wanted her to try. Needed to see that moment when her defiance cracked into something sweeter. Exhaling slowly, he rolled tension from his shoulders and lit a cigarette, the flame briefly illuminating his sharp features in the darkness. Her head snapped toward the light just as he extinguished it, but her gaze remained fixed where he stood. Even in the dark, he could see the fear behind those pretty eyes. He wondered what thoughts raced through that pretty head of hers.  

**Me:** *"The waiting is the best part, isn’t it? That delicious tension. The way your heart pounds when you wonder—*when?*"*  

*Soon.* But not yet. The anticipation was half the fun.
